title: A two-dimensional complex with embedding-dimension gap two
impact_reason: An exact separation e_PL=3 and e_lin=5 answers Brehm's minimum-dimension question in dimension two; the new step makes Newman's obstruction survive adaptive facet deletion, then uses the known PL embedding mechanism.
lay_summary: A surface-like finite object can be drawn without crossings in three dimensions if its faces may bend, yet needs five dimensions if every original face must stay flat.
surprise_reason: Bending faces changes the minimum dimension by two, already for two-dimensional complexes.
publication_reason: A short theorem with a precise named target, a self-contained deletion argument and explicit boundaries is a credible specialist submission.
exact_gap: No explicit facet list is produced; the enormous finite parameter choice is an existence certificate. Novelty against Newman and Lee–Nevo needs expert confirmation; this assessment does not validate the proof.
next_step: Submit the concise theorem with the deletion-resilience step and relation to the two antecedent mechanisms emphasized; retain the finite-bound checker as supplementary material.
claim_boundary: Finite simplicial complexes, without a manifold hypothesis; PL allows subdivision, whereas the linear invariant fixes the original simplices.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read; editorial assessment conditional on correctness and novelty, not a fresh proof or priority certification.

title: Irreducibility of exposed-point varieties of discotopes
impact_reason: Resolves the exposed-point irreducibility conjecture for arbitrary summand ranks at least two and the generic purely nonlinear-part conjecture; it also separates those varieties in nongeneric position.
lay_summary: For shapes made by adding ellipsoidal discs, all uniquely exposed boundary points belong to one indivisible algebraic shape, even when the discs overlap in special ways.
surprise_reason: A connected real-analytic parametrization settles a complex-algebraic irreducibility question without complex square-root branch analysis.
publication_reason: Two precisely sourced conjectural targets, an elementary mechanism and a useful nongeneric counterexample support a compact research article.
exact_gap: The proof imports the standard analytic identity-theorem mechanism and existing support parametrization. Historical priority and the relation to every existing discotope irreducibility theorem remain matters for specialist review.
next_step: Lead with the arbitrary-rank exposed-point theorem and keep the generic S(D)=E(D) identification explicit; submit with the nongeneric separating example.
claim_boundary: Every disc summand has dimension at least two; arbitrary nongeneric equality S(D)=E(D), degrees and birationality are not asserted.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read; no independent proof validation or fresh novelty search.

title: Nonattainment in the Harrell–Stubbe Dirichlet gap inequality
impact_reason: Settles finite-index saturation of a classical universal spectral gap bound and gives strict Yang inequality on every nonempty bounded open domain, with no regularity or connectedness assumption.
lay_summary: A famous estimate for gaps between a confined system's vibration frequencies can be approached but is never exactly reached at a finite frequency index.
surprise_reason: A short finite-spectral-support obstruction yields strictness even for irregular and disconnected domains.
publication_reason: The equality obstruction and clean domain scope form a plausible short spectral-theory paper, while the underlying commutator machinery is classical.
exact_gap: The result is a strictness/equality conclusion, not a quantitative positive deficit or improvement to leading Weyl asymptotics. Priority for strict Yang inequality needs specialist comparison.
next_step: Present as a short nonattainment theorem; keep the source's missing square and corrected scale-homogeneous formulation prominent.
claim_boundary: Form-defined Dirichlet Laplacian on bounded nonempty open Euclidean domains at finite index; no uniform positive deficit is established.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read; reported computations were not rerun and proof correctness was not independently certified.

title: Radial orthogonality does not imply dual 1-conformal flatness
impact_reason: Provides a transparent counterexample to a printed statistical-geometry implication, including a nowhere-zero cubic-tensor variant, but relies on classical Gauss-lemma and curvature facts.
lay_summary: Having nicely organized spheres around every point does not force the statistical geometry's dual connection to become flat under the proposed change of scale.
surprise_reason: The simple product S²×R defeats the implication through just two curvature evaluations.
publication_reason: A clear correction or short note is plausible, but elementary ingredients and explicitly unresolved historical priority weaken the case for a standalone full article.
exact_gap: The manuscript names uninspected Kurose, Binder–Simon and later Gauss-lemma sources; an earlier explicit or implicit answer cannot be excluded.
next_step: Resolve the listed priority leads and position the result as an explicit counterexample or explanatory note without claiming first resolution.
claim_boundary: Positive-definite statistical structures in dimension at least three; local 1-conformal flatness of the statistical connection, not ordinary metric conformal flatness; no cut-locus/global-foliation claim.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read, including its explicit unresolved-priority section; no new proof certification.

title: A note on Γ-supercyclicity of dissipative composition operators
impact_reason: Answers an arbitrary-Γ transfer question in the stated separable Lp setting, but the scalar criterion and amplification mechanism are explicitly consequences of Abbar and Abbar–Kuznetsova.
lay_summary: For this class of evolution operators, allowing any chosen set of scalar multipliers gives the same dense-orbit behavior as for a simpler weighted shift.
surprise_reason: The main value is making an existing theorem's application explicit, with separability as an essential boundary.
publication_reason: Useful explanatory application and scope correction, with limited added theorem content beyond the credited translation criteria.
exact_gap: A standalone originality case must rest on the specific composition-operator application, not repackage the established Γ criterion or amplification step as new.
next_step: Condense around the reported question and the conjugacy; consider a brief note or merge with broader composition-operator work.
claim_boundary: Separable complex Lp, 1≤p<∞, bounded invertible dissipative composition operators of bounded distortion; nonseparable σ-finite spaces are explicitly excluded.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read; dependencies identified from manuscript rather than a new source or proof audit.

title: The odd-part ratio under slow variation: a note on the printed Hilberdink problem
impact_reason: An elementary limiting theorem answers the literal printed question and corrects its local Euler constant, but does not address the plausible index-one intended reformulation.
lay_summary: For slowly growing weighted counts of integers, the fraction of weight on odd integers has an exact limit; the printed prediction uses the wrong local factor.
surprise_reason: The basic test f(n)=1/n turns the printed prediction 3/4 into the actual limit 1/2.
publication_reason: A crisp correction with a two-sided monotonicity argument is suitable for a note, with a modest independent contribution.
exact_gap: Originality may overlap elementary folklore or inaccessible factor-ratio literature; the possible regular-variation-index-one problem remains unaddressed.
next_step: Publish only the literal slow-variation statement and corrected constant, maintaining the explicit distinction from the possible intended question.
claim_boundary: Nonnegative nonzero multiplicative f with F(2x)/F(x)→1; reciprocal unweighted local Euler sum, including an infinite local sum and bounded F.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read; no fresh novelty assurance or computation replay.

title: Equality in the Fradelizi–Paouris–Schütt second-moment inequality
impact_reason: Extends a sharp inequality's equality classification from polytopes to all convex bodies through an extreme-point simplex partition and an exact nonnegative deficit identity.
lay_summary: Among convex bodies whose extreme points stay outside a sphere, the only shapes that exactly attain the moment bound are simplices with vertices on that sphere.
surprise_reason: A countable triangulation retains equality information that a naive limiting argument could lose.
publication_reason: A precise sourced conjecture, general-body equality rigidity and a finite strictness witness support a compact convex-geometry submission.
exact_gap: The inequality and simplex moment formula are credited to FPS; the new claim is equality for general bodies. This reading does not independently validate the countable partition or priority.
next_step: Emphasize the retained nonnegative deficit and finite two-simplex strictness witness; submit with the alternate finite-approximation proof available.
claim_boundary: Compact full-dimensional convex K and non-strict extreme-point norm bound; equality requires an inscribed nondegenerate simplex, not regularity or zero centroid.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read; editorial assessment only, conditional on correctness and novelty.

title: A coefficient normalization for positive definite forms
impact_reason: Resolves the ordered-coefficient coordinate-existence question for every positive definite homogeneous form, but permits arbitrarily ill-conditioned real changes of basis.
lay_summary: Any strictly positive even-degree form can be expressed in coordinates where pure coefficients are one and every mixed coefficient lies strictly between zero and one.
surprise_reason: A basis clustered near a minimizing direction forces simultaneous strict coefficient inequalities, even for nonconvex positive forms.
publication_reason: A short general theorem answering an explicit question has a plausible specialist venue; careful coefficient conventions are essential.
exact_gap: No quantitative conditioning, nonnegative-form, or integral/unimodular version follows. Priority and the exact Brandes convention need specialist confirmation.
next_step: Submit as a concise normalization theorem, showing the multinomial conversion and conditioning limitation near the statement.
claim_boundary: Strictly positive real homogeneous forms, even degree, real GL(m) changes; symmetric ordered coefficients rather than raw monomial coefficients.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read; no fresh correctness certification or novelty search.

title: A Lipschitz-nonincreasing deformation of small unitary-valued maps
impact_reason: Gives an explicit quantitative strong deformation retraction preserving the ≤1/2 Lipschitz sublevel in fixed U(N), refining the much easier classical logarithm-chart contraction.
lay_summary: A sufficiently slowly changing unitary-valued map on a sphere can be continuously flattened to a constant while its rate of change only decreases.
surprise_reason: A classical matrix fractional transform yields the exact global contraction factor (1−t²)/(1+t²) for two intrinsic length metrics.
publication_reason: The quantitative sublevel preservation, endpoint bound and parameter continuity are a plausible compact contribution beyond the classical local-contractibility mechanism.
exact_gap: The literal weak deformation question also follows from the classical principal logarithm. The submission's originality must concern the quantitative bound, not claim novelty for the Cayley transform or a general bi-invariant metric theorem.
next_step: Lead with the quantitative Lipschitz-preserving theorem for the two stated metrics and distinguish its added content from logarithm-chart contractibility.
claim_boundary: Unit-round spheres and unnormalized Hilbert–Schmidt or operator-norm length metrics on U(N), Lipschitz ≤1/2; constants retract onto U(N), not one prescribed constant.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read, including metric and S⁰ boundaries; no independent proof validation.

title: A four-vertex counterexample to Knudson's persistence-gradient conjecture
impact_reason: Refutes a precise persistence/discrete-Morse conjecture with a seven-simplex interval filtration; the distinction between fixed incident pairing and later cancellations is explicit.
lay_summary: Just four vertices on an interval show that a pairing found by persistence algebra need not correspond to any path in the proposed fixed discrete gradient.
surprise_reason: A conjectured unique path fails by having zero paths in the smallest-looking familiar one-dimensional setting, while an ordered cancellation creates the missing route.
publication_reason: A tiny checkable counterexample to a recorded conjecture is a credible short communication, with the fixed-field interpretation clearly protected.
exact_gap: No minimality is claimed and the reported audit leaves related work in preparation/inaccessible sources. The claim must remain about the fixed V_P field, not updated cancellation fields.
next_step: Submit as a short counterexample with the three column reductions and directed graph at the center; finish the bounded priority leads.
claim_boundary: Simplex-wise persistence pairing and incident submatching fixed before cancellation; works over every field, with no counterclaim to ordered-cancellation theorems.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read; small argument inspected editorially but no new verifier execution or complete novelty review.

title: A counterexample to Kourovka Notebook Problem 16.45
impact_reason: Constructs an explicit affine group with b_f=b=3<4=μ⁰, resolving the all-actions base-versus-independence question through a structural normality obstruction rather than only finite subgroup searches.
lay_summary: Two natural ways of measuring how many independent choices a finite group needs turn out to disagree, even after all nonfaithful actions are included.
surprise_reason: A central order-two subgroup of the complement ceases to be normal in the affine group; taking normal cores destroys the crucial four-way independence.
publication_reason: Precise invariant separation, an all-actions upper bound, explicit witnesses and independent exact implementations make a substantial specialist article.
exact_gap: The proof uses Cameron's established subgroup formulations; the complement classification and restriction argument require expert verification. No minimum-order result is supplied and this assessment has not rerun the certificates.
next_step: Prioritize specialist submission emphasizing the faithful/nonfaithful distinction and normal-bottom obstruction; supply both exact verifiers and the F11 boundary counterexample.
claim_boundary: One specified group F29²⋊SL2(5) of order 100920; bases are inclusion-minimal for the permutation image; not every characteristic yields the separation.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound manuscript read; no fresh proof certification, computation replay, or unconditional novelty assurance.

title: An explicit odd-order p-group with as many automorphisms as elements
impact_reason: Provides an explicit computer-assisted existence solution to Kourovka 16.63 with full automorphism count, combining an asymmetric lattice, a full-set log–exp bijection and exact Smith valuations; the rank-31 Lie template is credited to Omirov–Ruan.
lay_summary: There exists a finite group of odd prime-power size whose number of internal symmetries is exactly its number of elements, despite simple candidate families failing this equality.
surprise_reason: The full nonlinear automorphism-count problem is converted to a finite linear kernel count, then tuned to equality at an enormous but explicit group order.
publication_reason: A named existence problem, a genuinely structural full-automorphism argument and portable independent exact certificates support a serious specialist submission, subject to close expert checking.
exact_gap: The matrix calculation alone does not validate the finite-field stabilizer, lifting and integral log–exp steps; those analytic/algebraic lemmas are the central expert-review obligations. This assessment has not rerun certificates.
next_step: Prioritize a group-theory submission with the full-set bijection and the exact certificate's scope clearly separated; make the fast independent verifier prominent.
claim_boundary: One odd prime p=1009, order p^52359, class ≤846<p; no minimality, every-prime assertion, Cayley-table enumeration or proof-assistant certification.
review_basis: Complete checksum-bound 13-page manuscript read, including proof and computational-boundary sections; editorial conditional assessment only.
